### Functional Class Scoring

When comparing two biological conditions, are there entire biological processes that show coordinated differences in gene expression?

Cells under different biological conditions may express different sets of genes.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(DESeq2)
library(fgsea)
library(msigdbr)
```

```{r}

load(file='/home/projects/22140/exam_data/exam_functions.Rdata')

isoform_counts_GSE173955 <- loadIsoformCountMatrix("GSE173955")

gene_counts_GSE173955 <- extractGeneCountMatrixFromIsoCounts(isoform_counts_GSE173955)
meta_data_GSE173955 <- read.csv("data/metadata/GSE173955_metadata_clean.csv")


```

### Defining our biological comparison

```{r}
group_column <- "condition"
numerator <- "AD"
denominator <- "Control"

covariates <- covariates <- character(0)
```

### Get predefined gene sets on biological processes

```{r}
BP_df <- msigdbr(
  species = "human",
  collection = "C5",
  subcollection = "GO:BP"
)

BP_list <- split(
  BP_df$ensembl_gene,
  BP_df$gs_name
)
```

### Ranking the genes

Creating a spectrum of genes ranging from those with the strongest statistical evidence of upregulation to those with the strongest evidence of downregulation.

```{r}
myStats <- res_GSE173955$stat

names(myStats) <- rownames(res_GSE173955)

names(myStats) <- sub("\\.\\d+$", "", names(myStats))

myStats <- myStats[!is.na(myStats)]

myStats <- sort(myStats, decreasing = TRUE)
```

### Running Functional class scoring

```{r}
set.seed(42)

fg <- fgseaMultilevel(
  pathways = BP_list,
  stats = myStats,
  minSize = 15,
  maxSize = 500,
  scoreType = "std"
)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)

fg_sig <- fg |>
  arrange(padj) |>
  filter(padj < 0.05)

nrow(fg_sig)

head(fg_sig, 20)
```

Values to look at:

**ES: enrichment score**

Describes the observed distribution of genes belonging to a biological process within the ranked list.

A positive ES indicates enrichment towards the top, and a negative ES indicates enrichment towards the bottom.

**NES: Normalized enrichment score**

ES, but normalised

**PADJ: P-value adjusted for multiple testing**

How significance is ES?

```{r}
#choosing the most signicant one
chosen_pathway <- fg_sig$pathway[1]

plotEnrichment(
  BP_list[[chosen_pathway]],
  myStats
) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = chosen_pathway)
 # ggplot2::labs(title = paste0("Enrichment: ", chosen_pathway
```

```{r}
leading <- fg_sig$leadingEdge[[1]]

first_genes <- head(leading, 3)

first_genes
```
